answer: When a swarm operator tried to flood a summit vote, the velvet trick was volume: a thousand accounts whispering the same proposal. Slashing bonds stop that spiral at the wallet. Each identity locks 500 POA, unlocked only after six epochs; a panel catching duplicate work or copied answers burns the bond and resets it to zero. One fake risks 500 POA, so 1,000 fakes put 500,000 POA on the line for one vote, more than that vote pays. This defeats copy-paste sybil farms, because scale multiplies the stake instead of diluting it. Trade-off: newcomers must park capital before earning full weight.
